title: Graceful Nonce-Reuse Security for EPWC
summary: EPWC falls back to birthday-bound security once any nonce is repeated twice; the open task is to modify it so security degrades gracefully with maximum nonce multiplicity.

formal_statement.body: Construct a modification of the $\mathrm{EPWC}$ authentication mode whose security degrades gracefully as a function of the maximum number of repetitions of any nonce. The construction should avoid $\mathrm{EPWC}$'s current limitation, shared more generally by encrypted Wegman--Carter MACs, that security falls back to the birthday bound as soon as an adversary repeats even one nonce twice.

scope.domain: EPWC authentication modes and encrypted Wegman–Carter MACs under nonce reuse.
parameters: Maximum nonce multiplicity: governs the desired graceful degradation of security
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct an EPWC modification whose security degrades gracefully with maximum nonce multiplicity rather than immediately falling back to the birthday bound after a nonce is repeated twice.

citations.label: Counter-in-Tweak: Authenticated Encryption Modes for Tweakable Block Ciphers

progress.summary: The source explicitly presents graceful nonce-repetition security degradation for a modified EPWC mode as a pending question, contrasting it with EPWC's immediate fallback to birthday-bound security upon nonce reuse.
